svg.text: Encoder / embedding models on Spyre: target state
Model used: multilingual-e5-large · Compile Mode: True
Per-step serving path
vLLM Scheduler, used as-is
batches S requests carrying T tokens in total · chunked prefill off · never subclassed, its output never mutated
Token-count bucket dispatch
override of _determine_batch_execution_and_padding → round T up to the next compiled bucket, giving T_padded
upstream this hook pads to a captured CUDA graph; here to a compiled shape · pad rows zeroed · also cuts torch-spyre per-op recompiles
Compiled model body: one graph per token bucket (fullgraph, dynamic=False)
sees only the flat token list [T_padded, hidden], with no request boundaries · all layers share op shapes, so cost scales with distinct T, not with depth
Embeddings → N × [ Q · K · V projections (un-fused) · output projection · FFN ×2 · LayerNorm ×2 ]
N = 24 for multilingual-e5-large · 6 matrix multiplies per layer, 5 of them outside attention
torch.ops.vllm.unified_attention_with_output · opaque boundary
Dynamo does not trace inside. Selected by the platform's opaque_attention_op() → True, which TorchSpyrePlatform inherits from CpuPlatform
Encoder attention: the only request-aware stage
per-extent groups: requests sharing a padded length are served by one batched SDPA · gather, attend and store are one compiled graph
Row tables and masks, built once per step and carried on the attention metadata
one int32 row table and one [group, 1, 1, extent] mask per plan · derived from the per-request lengths, so identical for every layer
Fused kernel: gather → SDPA → store, one compiled graph
index_select the plan's rows into [group × extent, H, D] · batched SDPA · index_copy_ the result back
keyed on (buffer_rows, group, extent) · pad lanes clamp to the sequence's last real row, so no zero row is needed
tables on the metadata instead of rebuilt per layer · one launch per plan per layer, where the three-stage split cost three
Pooler on device: CLS / LAST / MEAN
row gather via index_select · L2 normalize via rsqrt · reads only real rows, using the per-request offsets
eager today · spyre_pooler.py subclasses the upstream poolers; compiling it is its own work item, not a warmup
MEAN copies packed [T, H] as fp16 and reduces on the host. Destagger of a device fp32 sum is garbage (torch-spyre#2971). #3507 would keep the reduce on the card.
Pooled vectors → host
only [num_reqs, hidden] crosses the boundary · padded rows are discarded, never pooled
Shape vocabulary
T · tokens in the step
sum of the batched prompt lengths · bucketed to 256 / 512 / 1024 / 2048 tokens
group · requests in one attention call
requests sharing an extent, in powers of two, capped by max_num_seqs
extent · one request's padded length
per request, not per step: its own length in 64-token units, rounded to a power of two
so a 260-token request attends over 512 · requests sharing an extent can be grouped
Worked example, prompts of 40, 12 and 58 tokens:
T = 110 → T_padded = 256 · every extent = 64 · group 3 chunks to 2 + 1, so two plans.
Compilation mode
CompilationMode.STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE
torch.compile(model, backend="inductor",
fullgraph=True, dynamic=False)
dynamic=False → sizes are baked in as constants. A graph built for
128 tokens works only for 128; a new count means a new compile.
Startup: warmup walks every bucket set
for T in token buckets: _dummy_run(T)
one compiled body graph per bucket
_warm_kernels, called from forward
sweeps (extent, group) on the first call per buffer_rows · the dummy
runs cannot span it: an extent follows the request, not the bucket
_dummy_pooler_run + _warm_pooler_row_widths
pooler cost follows the request count, so row widths are swept too
warms
Design invariants
· The attention metadata always describes the real batch, so no
padded row is ever gathered into a request or pooled.
· Padding the body is safe because each layer treats every token
row on its own.
Attention shape strategy: the per-extent groups used above, and how flash attention would change it
A · Per-extent groups, the strategy shown above
Gather each group's rows out of the flat list into a dense batch, so every shape is
fixed at compile time. Needed because an offset computed from data does not lower
under compilation (torch-spyre#3508) — exactly the arithmetic flash relies on.
Eager tolerates it; compiled mode, our target, does not.
· group the step's requests by padded length, so each plan has one extent
· one compiled graph per plan does gather, SDPA and store together
· mask is [group, 1, 1, extent]; head and query axes broadcast
Shape axes: T for the body, (buffer_rows, group, extent) for attention.
Costs: the pack is still paid, and fusion put buffer_rows into the attention key.
Cheaper than masking a block-diagonal over the flat list. Current implementation.
B · Flash-style attention, planned
Never materialise the batch. Each block of queries reads its request's offset from the
metadata at runtime and works directly on the flat list, carrying a running softmax maximum
and sum — the online-softmax structure the Spyre decoder path already uses over KV pages.
· no [group, 1, 1, extent] mask; request boundaries are the offsets
· no gather or store; the kernel reads the flat list directly
· extent disappears, replaced by a block count
Two separate prerequisites, often conflated:
· torch-spyre#3508, data-dependent offsets → flat-list attention, coarse block count
· symbolic shapes (the backend rejects SymInt today) → no bucketing on any axis
With #3508 alone the block count stays bucketed, as the decoder's page loop is.
If flash attention lands, what changes — and what fusion already changed:
· attention stops gathering, so the pack and its launch go away; extent collapses to a coarser block count
· the mask disappears entirely; request boundaries become offsets read at runtime
What fusion already did, and what it cost: collapsing gather, SDPA and store into one graph removed two launches
per plan per layer, but pulled buffer_rows into the attention key. The branch moved toward flash's shape while moving
away from its single axis. Flash would not remove buffer_rows either — attention still writes the body-sized buffer.
Unchanged either way: the padding seam, metadata describing the real batch, warmup coverage, compilation mode.
